output.scope_note: The paper reports room-temperature Li-ion conductivities of halide solid electrolytes Li3YCl6-xBrx, computed from fine-tuned CHGNet MD in this work, plus one literature-cited experimental value.

records.measurement_method: NVT MD with Nernst-Einstein relation (CHGNet_600K, 1 bar cells)
records.evidence_quote: For 1 bar-equilibrated cells, we obtain EA = 0.12 ± 0.01 eV (0.25 ± 0.01 eV) and σ300K ∼ 331 mS.cm−1 (∼ 20 mS.cm−1 ) for LYC (LYB)
records.notes: Value is the predicted sigma(300K) for LYC from MD at 1 bar equilibrated volume; the paper says it is overestimated relative to experiment. Temperature given as sigma300K subscript.

records.measurement_method: NVT MD with Nernst-Einstein relation (CHGNet_600K, 1 bar cells)
records.evidence_quote: For 1 bar-equilibrated cells, we obtain EA = 0.12 ± 0.01 eV (0.25 ± 0.01 eV) and σ300K ∼ 331 mS.cm−1 (∼ 20 mS.cm−1 ) for LYC (LYB)
records.notes: Approximate value ('∼ 20') from text; Table 2 lists 19.5 (15.4; 35.1) for CHGNet_600K 1 bar. Value taken from the text quote.

records.measurement_method: NVT MD with Nernst-Einstein relation (CHGNet_600K, cells equilibrated at 10 kbar)
records.evidence_quote: Li-ion mobility decreases, yielding EA = 0.24 ± 0.01 eV (0.36 ± 0.02 eV) and σ300K ∼ 15.7 mS.cm−1 (∼ 0.6 mS.cm−1 ) for LYC (LYB)
records.notes: Computed at p = 10 kbar (cells compressed toward experimental volume); the paper treats this as the more realistic value.

records.measurement_method: NVT MD with Nernst-Einstein relation (CHGNet_600K, cells equilibrated at 10 kbar)
records.evidence_quote: Li-ion mobility decreases, yielding EA = 0.24 ± 0.01 eV (0.36 ± 0.02 eV) and σ300K ∼ 15.7 mS.cm−1 (∼ 0.6 mS.cm−1 ) for LYC (LYB)
records.notes: Computed at p = 10 kbar; Table 2 gives 0.58 (0.37; 1.66) for this case. Value taken from the text quote.

records.evidence_quote: van der Maas et al. observed in the Li3 YCl6−x Brx (LYCB) series that ionic conductivity peaks at 5.36 mS cm−1 near x = 4.5.
records.notes: Experimental value from Ref. 9 (van der Maas et al.), cited in the introduction; measurement temperature not stated in this paper. Peak conductivity across the series at x near 4.5.
